newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates unchanged in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates unchanged in liquid market.

text.p: Manila overnight rates were unchanged at an average of 11.0625 percent on Friday as banks continued to enjoy ample liquidity, traders said.
"Nothing's happening to make the market change. The Central Bank is not moving on the dollar and peso," a foreign bank dealer said.
Traders said the Central Bank had stayed out of the foreign exchange market for two days.
The Central Bank's purchases or sales of dollars would have an impact on peso liquidity.
Market volume was lower at 12.772 billion from 19.770 billion pesos, with 21 lenders and 23 borrowers.
The Central Bank kept its overnight lending and borrowing rates at 15 and 11 percent respectively.
At the secondary market trading of T-bills, "nothing's moving. There is no urgency to go into government securities," said a dealer.
Traders said banks continue to be cautious about the possible tightness arising from Christmas spending.
"No one wants to be short of pesos by the end of the year," said the same dealer.
Traders said the three-month bills were quoted an offer rate of 11.60 to 11.70 percent; the six months at 12.15 to 12.25; and the one year at 12.65 to 12.70.
